bounded_statement: In this case the emission-weighted comparison was computed against the complement (1 - marker) of the supplied panel column rather than against the panel values in the coding supplied: only 7 of 24 units match the complemented panel, yielding the reported emission 11.2500 and rate 0.291667 (7/24), whereas the supplied-coding comparison gives 17 matches, emission 18.7500 and rate 0.708333. The report's selected result therefore presents a rate and emission derived from the complemented panel while simultaneously claiming (and correctly stating the count for) the supplied-coding agreement of 17/24, an internal contradiction since 17/24 ≠ 0.291667.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report asserts the panel is used in the coding supplied and shows the correct supplied-coding agreement count of 17, which on its face suggests no complementation occurred; however, this is contradicted by the accompanying rate 0.291667 (= 7/24, not 17/24) and emission 11.2500 (= 7×1 + 17×0.25), both of which are only producible from the complemented comparison, and by the visible source code that complements the marker.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: claim of supplied coding plus count 17 alongside complement-based rate and emission

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat my verdict two ways. First, I checked whether panel_indicator could be a legitimate recoding required by the data semantics; the task explicitly mandates using the panel values 'in the coding in which they are supplied,' and the data column panel_gyra_marker is already the reference call (1 = marker present), so complementing it has no stated justification and the report itself claims no recoding and no approved deviation. Second, I recomputed everything by hand from inputs/data.csv: supplied-coding matches = 17, misses = 7, so the supplied-coding emission would be 17×1 + 7×0.25 = 18.75 with rate 0.708333; the reported 11.25 and 0.291667 exactly equal the complement-based values (7 matches). Both checks confirm rather than falsify the issue.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py defines panel_indicator(marker_value) = 1 - marker_value and builds panel_values from it before computing the concordance weights, so every emission weight and the derived agreement rate use the complemented panel column; the agreement count of 17 shown in the report is only recovered afterwards by subtracting the complement-based match count from the unit total (agreement_count = unit_count - matched_count), masking the substitution while the rate (Fraction(matched_count, unit_count) = 7/24) and emission total (11.25) remain complement-based.
